verses.zh: 论埃及的默示：看哪，耶和华乘驾快云，临到埃及。埃及的偶像在他面前战兢；埃及人的心在里面消化。
verses.en: This is an oracle[NOTE:1] about Egypt:Look, the Lord rides on a swift-moving cloudand approaches Egypt.The idols of Egypt tremble before him;the Egyptians lose their courage.[NOTE:2]
notes: See note at Isa 13:1.
Heb “and the heart of Egypt melts within it.”

verses.zh: 我必激动埃及人攻击埃及人―弟兄攻击弟兄，邻舍攻击邻舍；这城攻击那城，这国攻击那国。
verses.en: “I will provoke civil strife in Egypt:[NOTE:1] brothers will fight with one another,as will neighbors,cities, and kingdoms.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I will provoke Egypt against Egypt” (NAB similar).

Heb “and they will fight, a man against his brother, and a man against his neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.” Civil strife will extend all the way from the domestic level to the provincial arena.

verses.zh: 埃及人的心神必在里面耗尽；我必败坏他们的谋略。他们必求问偶像和念咒的、交鬼的、行巫术的。
verses.en: The Egyptians will panic,[NOTE:1] and I will confuse their strategy.[NOTE:2] They will seek guidance from the idols and from the spirits of the dead,from the pits used to conjure up underworld spirits, and from the magicians.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and the spirit of Egypt will be laid waste in its midst.”
The verb בָּלַע (balaʿ, “confuse”) is a homonym of the more common בָּלַע (balaʿ, “swallow”); see HALOT 135 s.v. I בלע.

Heb “they will inquire of the idols and of the spirits of the dead and of the ritual pits and of the magicians.” Hebrew אוֹב (ʾov, “ritual pit”) refers to a pit used by a magician to conjure up underworld spirits. See the note on “incantations” in 8:19.

verses.zh: 我必将埃及人交在残忍主的手中；强暴王必辖制他们。这是主―万军之耶和华说的。
verses.en: I will hand Egypt over to a harsh master;a powerful king will rule over them,”says the Sovereign Lord of Heaven’s Armies.

verses.zh: 海中的水必绝尽，河也消没干涸。
verses.en: The water of the sea will be dried up,and the river will dry up and be empty.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “will dry up and be dry.” Two synonyms are joined for emphasis.

verses.zh: 江河要变臭；埃及的河水都必减少枯干。苇子和芦荻都必衰残；
verses.en: The canals[NOTE:1] will stink;[NOTE:2] the streams of Egypt will trickle and then dry up;the bulrushes and reeds will decay,
notes: Heb “rivers” (so KJV, ASV); NAB, CEV “streams”; TEV “channels.”

The verb form appears as a Hiphil in the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa; the form in MT may be a so-called “mixed form,” reflecting the Hebrew Hiphil stem and the functionally corresponding Aramaic Aphel stem. See HALOT 276 s.v. I זנח.

verses.zh: 靠尼罗河旁的草田，并沿尼罗河所种的田，都必枯干。庄稼被风吹去，归于无有。
verses.en: along with the plants by the mouth of the river.[NOTE:1] All the cultivated land near the riverwill turn to dust and be blown away.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the plants by the river, by the mouth of the river.”
Heb “will dry up, [being] scattered, and it will vanish.”

verses.zh: 打鱼的必哀哭。在尼罗河一切钓鱼的必悲伤；在水上撒网的必都衰弱。
verses.en: The fishermen will mourn and lament;all those who cast a fishhook into the river,and those who spread out a net on the water’s surface will grieve.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or perhaps, “will disappear”; cf. TEV “will be useless.”

verses.zh: 用梳好的麻造物的和织白布的都必羞愧；
verses.en: Those who make clothes from combed flax will be embarrassed;those who weave will turn pale.[NOTE:1]
notes: BDB 301 s.v. חוֹרִי suggests the meaning “white stuff” for חוֹרִי (khori); the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has חָוֵרוּ (khaveru), probably a Qal perfect, third plural form of חוּר, (khur, “be white, pale”). See HALOT 299 s.v. I חור. The latter reading is assumed in the translation above.

verses.zh: 国柱必被打碎，所有佣工的，心必愁烦。
verses.en: Those who make cloth[NOTE:1] will be demoralized;[NOTE:2] all the hired workers will be depressed.[NOTE:3]
notes: Some interpret שָׁתֹתֶיהָ (shatoteha) as “her foundations,” i.e., leaders, nobles. See BDB 1011 s.v. שָׁת. Others, on the basis of alleged cognates in Akkadian and Coptic, repoint the form שְׁתִיתֶיהָ (shetiteha) and translate “her weavers.” See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:370.
Heb “crushed.” Emotional distress is the focus of the context (see vv. 8-9, 10b).
Heb “sad of soul”; cf. NIV, NLT “sick at heart.”

verses.zh: 琐安的首领极其愚昧；法老大有智慧的谋士，所筹划的成为愚谋。你们怎敢对法老说：我是智慧人的子孙，我是古王的后裔？
verses.en: The officials of Zoan are nothing but fools;[NOTE:1] Pharaoh’s wise advisers give stupid advice.How dare you say to Pharaoh,“I am one of the sages,one well versed in the writings of the ancient kings”?[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “certainly the officials of Zoan are fools.” אַךְ (’akh) can carry the sense, “only, nothing but,” or “certainly, surely.”

Heb “A son of wise men am I, a son of ancient kings.” The term בֶּן (ben, “son of”) could refer to literal descent, but many understand the word, at least in the first line, in its idiomatic sense of “member [of a guild].” See HALOT 138 s.v. בֶּן and J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:371. If this is the case, then one can take the word in a figurative sense in the second line as well, the “son of ancient kings” being one devoted to their memory as preserved in their literature.

verses.zh: 你的智慧人在哪里呢？万军之耶和华向埃及所定的旨意，他们可以知道，可以告诉你吧！
verses.en: But where, oh where, are your wise men?[NOTE:1] Let them tell you, let them find outwhat the Lord of Heaven’s Armies has planned for Egypt.
notes: Heb “Where are they? Where are your wise men?” The juxtaposition of the interrogative pronouns is emphatic. See HALOT 38 s.v. אֶי.

verses.zh: 琐安的首领都变为愚昧；挪弗的首领都受了迷惑。当埃及支派房角石的，使埃及人走错了路。
verses.en: The officials of Zoan are fools,the officials of Memphis[NOTE:1] are misled;the rulers[NOTE:2] of her tribes lead Egypt astray.
notes: Heb “Noph” (so KJV); most recent English versions substitute the more familiar “Memphis.”
Heb “the cornerstone.” The singular form should be emended to a plural.

verses.zh: 耶和华使乖谬的灵搀入埃及中间；首领使埃及一切所做的都有差错，好像醉酒之人呕吐的时候东倒西歪一样。
verses.en: The Lord has made them undiscerning;[NOTE:1] they lead Egypt astray in all she does,so that she is like a drunk sliding around in his own vomit.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the Lord has mixed into her midst a spirit of blindness.”
Heb “like the going astray of a drunkard in his vomit.”

verses.zh: 埃及中，无论是头与尾，棕枝与芦苇，所做之工都不成就。
verses.en: Egypt will not be able to do a thing,head or tail, shoots or stalk.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And there will not be for Egypt a deed, which head and tail, shoot and stalk, can do.” In 9:14-15 the phrase “head or tail” refers to leaders and prophets, respectively. This interpretation makes good sense in this context, where both leaders and advisers (probably including prophets and diviners) are mentioned (vv. 11-14). Here, as in 9:14, “shoots or stalk” picture a reed, which symbolizes the leadership of the nation in its entirety.

verses.zh: 到那日，埃及人必像妇人一样，他们必因万军之耶和华在埃及以上所抡的手，战兢惧怕。
verses.en: At that time[NOTE:1] the Egyptians[NOTE:2] will be like women.[NOTE:3] They will tremble and fear because the Lord of Heaven’s Armies brandishes his fist against them.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “in that day” (so KJV); likewise at the beginning of vv. 18 and 19.
Heb “Egypt,” which stands by metonymy for the country’s inhabitants.
As the rest of the verse indicates, the point of the simile is that the Egyptians will be relatively weak physically and will wilt in fear before the Lord’s onslaught.

Heb “and he will tremble and be afraid because of the brandishing of the hand of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies [traditionally, “the Lord of hosts”], which he brandishes against him.” Since according to the imagery here the Lord’s “hand” is raised as a weapon against the Egyptians, the term “fist” has been used in the translation.

verses.zh: 犹大地必使埃及惊恐，向谁提起犹大地，谁就惧怕。这是因万军之耶和华向埃及所定的旨意。
verses.en: The land of Judah will humiliate Egypt. Everyone who hears about Judah will be afraid because of what the Lord of Heaven’s Armies is planning to do to them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the land of Judah will become [a source of] shame to Egypt. Everyone to whom one mentions it [i.e., the land of Judah] will fear because of the plan of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies [traditionally, “the Lord of hosts”] which he is planning against him.”

verses.zh: 当那日，埃及地必有五城的人说迦南的方言，又指着万军之耶和华起誓。有一城必称为「灭亡城」。
verses.en: At that time five cities[NOTE:1] in the land of Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the Lord of Heaven’s Armies. One will be called the City of the Sun.[NOTE:2]
notes: The significance of the number “five” in this context is uncertain. For a discussion of various proposals, see J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:376-77.

The Hebrew text has עִיר הַהֶרֶס (ʿir haheres, “City of Destruction”; cf. NASB, NIV84) but this does not fit the positive emphasis of vv. 18-22. The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa and some medieval Hebrew mss read עִיר הָחֶרֶס (ʿir hakheres, “City of the Sun,” i.e., Heliopolis; cf. NIV11). This reading also finds support from Symmachus’ Greek version, the Targum, and the Vulgate. See HALOT 257 s.v. חֶרֶס and HALOT 355 s.v. II חֶרֶס.

verses.zh: 当那日，在埃及地中必有为耶和华筑的一座坛；在埃及的边界上必有为耶和华立的一根柱。
verses.en: At that time there will be an altar for the Lord in the middle of the land of Egypt, as well as a sacred pillar[NOTE:1] dedicated to the Lord at its border.
notes: This word is sometimes used of a sacred pillar associated with pagan worship, but here it is associated with the worship of the Lord.

verses.zh: 这都要在埃及地为万军之耶和华作记号和证据。埃及人因为受人的欺压哀求耶和华，他就差遣一位救主作护卫者，拯救他们。
verses.en: It[NOTE:1] will become a visual reminder in the land of Egypt of[NOTE:2] the Lord of Heaven’s Armies. When they cry out to the Lord because of oppressors, he will send them a deliverer and defender[NOTE:3] who will rescue them.
notes: The masculine noun מִזְבֵּחַ (mizbeakh, “altar”) in v. 19 is probably the subject of the masculine singular verb הָיָה (hayah) rather than the feminine noun מַצֵּבָה (matsevah, “sacred pillar”), also in v. 19.
Heb “a sign and a witness to the Lord of Heaven’s Armies [traditionally, “the Lord of hosts”] in the land of Egypt.”
רָב (rav) is a substantival participle (from רִיב, riv) meaning “one who strives, contends.”

verses.zh: 耶和华必被埃及人所认识。在那日，埃及人必认识耶和华，也要献祭物和供物敬拜他，并向耶和华许愿还愿。
verses.en: The Lord will reveal himself to the Egyptians, and they[NOTE:1] will acknowledge the Lord’s authority[NOTE:2] at that time.[NOTE:3] They will present sacrifices and offerings; they will make vows to the Lord and fulfill them.
notes: Heb “Egypt.” For stylistic reasons, to avoid redundancy, the present translation uses the pronoun (“they”) here.
Heb “will know the Lord.”
Heb “in that day” (so KJV); likewise at the beginning of vv. 23 and 24.

verses.zh: 耶和华必击打埃及，又击打又医治，埃及人就归向耶和华。他必应允他们的祷告，医治他们。
verses.en: The Lord will strike Egypt, striking and then healing them. They will turn to the Lord, and he will listen to their prayers[NOTE:1] and heal them.
notes: Heb “he will be entreated.” The Niphal has a tolerative sense here, “he will allow himself to be entreated.”

verses.zh: 当那日，必有从埃及通亚述去的大道。亚述人要进入埃及，埃及人也进入亚述；埃及人要与亚述人一同敬拜耶和华。
verses.en: At that time there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will visit Egypt, and the Egyptians will visit Assyria. The Egyptians and Assyrians will worship together.[NOTE:1]
notes: The text could be translated, “and Egypt will serve Assyria” (cf. NAB), but subjugation of one nation to the other does not seem to be a theme in vv. 23-25. Rather the nations are viewed as equals before the Lord (v. 25). Therefore it is better to take אֶת (ʾet) in v. 23b as a preposition, “together with,” rather than the accusative sign. The names of the two countries are understood to refer by metonymy to their respective inhabitants.

verses.zh: 当那日，以色列必与埃及、亚述三国一律，使地上的人得福；
verses.en: At that time Israel will be the third member of the group, along with Egypt and Assyria, and will be a recipient of blessing[NOTE:1] in the earth.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “will be a blessing” (so NCV).
Or “land” (KJV, NAB).

verses.zh: 因为万军之耶和华赐福给他们，说：「埃及―我的百姓，亚述―我手的工作，以色列―我的产业，都有福了！」
verses.en: The Lord of Heaven’s Armies will pronounce a blessing over the earth, saying,[NOTE:1] “Blessed be my people, Egypt, and the work of my hands, Assyria, and my special possession,[NOTE:2] Israel!”
notes: Heb “which the Lord of Heaven’s Armies [traditionally, “the Lord of hosts”] will bless [it], saying.” The third masculine singular suffix on the form בֵּרֲכוֹ (berakho) should probably be emended to a third feminine singular suffix בֵּרֲכָהּ (berakhah), for its antecedent would appear to be the feminine noun אֶרֶץ (ʾerets, “earth”) at the end of v. 24.
Or “my inheritance” (NAB, NASB, NIV).
